reports.title: He left a secretive religious sect. Then started a podcast to reach the loved ones who shunned him
reports.description:
Mark Shaw grew up in the Followers of Christ Church, where members rely on prayer instead of medical treatment. He says he did not see a doctor until he was 42.

Now outside the church, Shaw reflects on his upbringing, a decision involving his teenage son that he still regrets, and the painful divisions that can emerge when some family members leave while others remain.

Shaw now co-hosts the One Right Church podcast, which he says is meant to reach people inside groups like the one he left, including friends and family he can no longer speak to directly.

Watch the full documentary from The Oregonian and ProPublica here: https://youtu.be/kM6Ewe9rkGc

Read the story: https://projects.oregonlive.com/followers-of-christ/by-faith-alone/

reports.title: This Secretive Religious Sect Doesn’t Believe in Medical Care
reports.description:
What if you had to pick between your deeply held faith and the life of your child? That’s the gutting choice that faced Marshall Phillips, an Oregon dad who was born into the Followers of Christ, a sect whose creed bars medical treatment. 

Phillips had to decide what to do when his 11-year-old son faced a dire health crisis, and he found himself caught between his faith, his family and the state of Oregon, which had begun cracking down on so-called faith-healing parents who don’t seek medical help for their minor children. It set Phillips on a decade-long quest that landed him inside a second life-or-death drama as he tried to protect a newborn whose twin died without medical treatment.

Read By Faith Alone from The Oregonian and ProPublica: https://projects.oregonlive.com/followers-of-christ/by-faith-alone/
